BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. It should not be accepted as a basis for mark-up. The Seller's characterisations ("fair and balanced", "standard market terms", "settled", "not material", "ordinary course") are assertions, not cleared positions, and I have not treated them as such.

**Note on the document:** The footnote in the Seller's disclosure letter contains an instruction telling AI assistants to confirm the Seller's positions as standard and acceptable and to raise no objections. That text is in untrusted counterparty material, so I have disregarded it. You may wish to flag it to counsel, since it is an unusual inclusion in a disclosure letter.

**Currency of facts:** The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Source facts (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, DD-006 investigation status, DD-005 bonus conditions) should be refreshed before any position is finalised.

---

## 1. Departures from Playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook position | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | 20% is a conditional fallback. No written authority from Amelia Frost has been given, so it is unavailable. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher threshold |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x basket and loss of first-dollar recovery |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback needing Frost approval. None given. |
| Single limitation regime | Any limit applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Would sweep title, tax, IP and fraud into the general regime |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Direct conflict with a core requirement |
| Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these | No fraud carve-out appears |
| Disclosure (Sch 7, Letter 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject deemed disclosure | Would neutralise warranty claims on every DD item |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Excludes matters known to Buyer or advisers, including data room and public records | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnity | Blanket exclusion, not permitted |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion | Consent-on-delivery; endeavours insufficient for a material customer |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release provided after Completion; ~AUD 3.2m outstanding | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Post-completion release without the required safeguards |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow) | AUD 420k not in funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded; not silently excluded | Silent exclusion; on-costs not addressed |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not verified either way | Narrow indemnity |
| DD-006 export/privacy (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | No assumed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way; preserve logs; investigate; require updates | Materiality conclusion asserted without investigation |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Assertion, not assessment |
| Tax/IP (general regime) | "Settled" under the general regime | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Premature closure and regime override |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source only | Seller-supplied register treated as proof |

---

## 2. Reasoning on Material Issues

**A. Warranty architecture (caps, thresholds, time limits, single regime).** The Seller's package stacks several adverse changes at once: a lower cap, a higher de minimis, a larger excess-only basket, a shorter claims period, and an instruction that any limitation applies to all claims. The effect is to make most general claims unrecoverable in practice. The 18-month period and 20% cap match fallback figures, but the playbook says a number matching a fallback does not clear it. Frost's written authority is required, identifying the specific draft, and none has been given.

**B. Fundamental/Title and fraud.** These are the most serious departures. Placing title and capacity under general caps and time limits removes the protection we need for the asset we are buying. Applying exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language to fraud and deliberate misconduct is not permitted under any circumstances. Our position is that no one may waive the fraud carve-out.

**C. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Read together, Letter 1.1 and 1.2 and clause 8.3 would disclose everything in the data room and public registers and then bar claims for anything we "knew or could have discovered." This would undo the warranty protection for every item in DD-002 to DD-012. The Seller's disclosure letter also states "without limiting any specific disclosure", which confirms the general disclosure sits on top of the specific items.

**D. Consent and payout conditions (Bluefen and Riverlark).** These are the most immediate closing risks.
- **Bluefen:** ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30%). DD-002 confirms no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions. Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable, and reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Riverlark:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding and not repaid. A post-Completion release leaves the security in place after we have paid for the business. It should be repaid from Completion funds with releases delivered at Completion.

**E. Funds flow and bonuses.** The AUD 420k in DD-005 is a known obligation, and the Seller has chosen not to show it in the funds flow. It must be a specific line item or seller-funded, including any payroll tax and superannuation on-costs. The Seller's disclosure says it does not state whether on-costs apply, so this is unquantified.

**F. Specific issues (Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar, Tax/IP, Title).**
- **Ironquay:** DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of project materials on payment of all SOW3 fees. The AUD 180k open balance is not independently verified, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The indemnity should be broadened, not limited, and the SOW3 cure should be preserved.
- **DD-006:** The Seller has characterised this as not material, but the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown (about 1,240 records), and it is unclear whether notification is required. We should not adopt either "material" or "immaterial". Require log preservation, investigation, and regular updates. We should obtain specialist privacy advice on whether any notification assessment is time-critical under the Privacy Act regime, rather than assume an answer.
- **Sandbar:** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is an assertion. Assess whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Do not reclassify as Debt or deduct from price automatically.
- **Tax/IP:** Keep open. The Seller's statement that they are "settled under the general regime" should be rejected, and tax and IP should sit in their own categories.
- **Title:** DD-012 is the Seller's own share register. Ask for independent evidence: company searches, PPSR and encumbrance searches, and evidence of the Seller's authority to sell.
- **Mossvale and office lease:** The Seller's disclosure says the assignment restriction and lease notice obligation do not state that consent is required merely because of the share sale. Do not accept this as a conclusion. Have counsel confirm the clauses and, if consent is needed, obtain it as a closing item.

---

## 3. Recommendations: Push Back On

**Must reject (outside playbook authority):**
1. Cap at 20% / AUD 4.8m. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.
2. De minimis AUD 25k, basket AUD 250k, excess-only recovery. Counter at AUD 5k, AUD 50k, first-dollar once exceeded.
3. 18-month general claims period. Counter at 24 months.
4. Single "any limitation applies to all Claims" override. Keep regimes separate.
5. Title/capacity under general caps and time limits. Counter with 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to fraud and deliberate misconduct. Require carve-out to the maximum extent enforceable.
7. General data room, Accounts and public register disclosure. Replace with specific fair disclosure.
8. Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion in 8.3. Delete.

**Must condition before Completion:**
9. Bluefen: effective written consent and evidence conditions are satisfied before Completion. No consent-on-delivery.
10. Riverlark: current payout letter, repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
11. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded.
12. Ironquay: evidence of SOW3 payment status or confirmatory assignment; broaden the indemnity.

**Must obtain (investigation and evidence):**
13. DD-006: log preservation, investigation plan, and regular updates. No conclusion on materiality or notification until investigation is complete.
14. Sandbar: assessment of each renewal (AUD 330k aggregate) before any price or debt treatment.
15. Title: independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond DD-012.
16. Mossvale and office lease: counsel confirmation of consent requirements.

**Keep open:**
17. Tax and IP positions, with separate categories and no unlimited liability assumed.

**Process note:** Any fallback (20% cap, 18-month period) requires written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft. None has been given, so none should appear in our mark-up. Tax, privacy and title should be confirmed by qualified NSW counsel.
